entries.text: Revenue = SUM(orders.final_amount) over orders with order_status = 'Delivered'. final_amount is the amount after discount (total_amount - discount_amount). Do not use orders.total_amount or payments.amount for revenue.
entries.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) = 0 FROM orders WHERE ABS(final_amount - (total_amount - discount_amount)) > 0.005

entries.text: A restaurant's rating = AVG(ratings.rating) over its rows in ratings (join on restaurant_id). restaurants.avg_rating is a stored value that differs from that average for every restaurant (by more than 0.05); do not use it unless the question asks for the stored value.
entries.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM restaurants) FROM restaurants r JOIN (SELECT restaurant_id, AVG(rating) AS a FROM ratings GROUP BY restaurant_id) g ON g.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id WHERE ABS(r.avg_rating - g.a) > 0.05

entries.text: orders.order_status is one of Placed, Preparing, Out for Delivery, Delivered, Cancelled. "Not cancelled" means order_status <> 'Cancelled'. Use orders.order_status for the status of an order; order_tracking holds the status-update history.
entries.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) = 0 FROM orders WHERE order_status NOT IN ('Placed', 'Preparing', 'Out for Delivery', 'Delivered', 'Cancelled')

entries.text: A payment is successful when payments.payment_status = 'Success' (other values: Pending, Failed, Refunded). Each order has exactly one payment (payments.order_id).
entries.check_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments WHERE payment_status = 'Success') > 0 AND (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT payment_status) FROM payments) = 3 AND (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FROM payments) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders)

entries.text: An order used a coupon when orders.coupon_id IS NOT NULL; the coupon is the coupons row with coupon_id = orders.coupon_id.
entries.check_sql: SELECT SUM(coupon_id IS NOT NULL) > 0 AND SUM(coupon_id IS NULL) > 0 FROM orders

entries.text: A customer's default address is the customer_addresses row with is_default = 1; every customer has exactly one.
entries.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) = 0 FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM customer_addresses GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(is_default = 1) <> 1)

entries.text: Flag columns hold 1 (true) or 0 (false): menu_items.is_veg, menu_items.is_available, and is_active on customers, restaurants, delivery_partners and coupons.
entries.check_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM menu_items WHERE is_veg NOT IN (0, 1) OR is_available NOT IN (0, 1)) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE is_active NOT IN (0, 1)) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM restaurants WHERE is_active NOT IN (0, 1)) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delivery_partners WHERE is_active NOT IN (0, 1)) + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coupons WHERE is_active NOT IN (0, 1)) = 0

entries.text: Ratings exist only for delivered orders, at most one per order (ratings.order_id).
entries.check_sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ratings g JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = g.order_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'Delivered') = 0 AND (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) FROM ratings) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ratings)

entries.text: menu_items.created_at is always NULL (not populated); never filter, sort or group by it.
Names: customers.full_name, delivery_partners.full_name, restaurants.name, menu_items.item_name, categories.category_name.
order_items is the bridge between orders and menu_items (order_items.order_id -> orders, order_items.item_id -> menu_items). order_items.subtotal = quantity * price_at_order.
Both orders.restaurant_id and menu_items.restaurant_id reference restaurants. An order's customer is orders.customer_id; its delivery address is orders.address_id -> customer_addresses.

sections.title: Ambiguities (ask which is meant unless the question says)

entries.text: city exists in customer_addresses, restaurants and delivery_partners with no default; ask which city is meant.
